items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: I was with Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band when we made that recording.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. I was with Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band when we made that recording. I knew Ma Rainey because I sat in the Bijou Theater playing shows with the pit band. I wasn’t getting paid, I did it because they let me do it. And I just did it to try to learn as much as I could. And Ma Rainey, she came, she was the ugliest blues singer on earth when she got old, but when she was young she was pretty. You see her picture, she was the prettiest, nice looking girl. But she is so ugly, that that’s what they call the…

items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: there was two of the original members of my band, when I had my band, when I had my band here, Dreamlin in his band, it was Doc Cheatham, Adolph Cheatham, and Jerry Blake, see.

ctx.x: Now just a couple of minutes if you can tell about your European trip, unless there's something else you can think of too you'd like to tell about.

Well, the European trip was, it was very interesting. I enjoyed it very much. The act that, I went over to join an act that had, it was a dancing act, a Spanish act, and they had a band with them, an American band. I only knew one fellow in the band, Spallin, he was a pianist, had been with the original Jimmy Wade band. So they sent for me, in fact they sent for two of us from Chicago, they sent for Clifford King and myself. And doing the transaction, which it takes quite a bit of transaction, it did at that time…
